base: OK      beta \[optional\]: present \(jq\)\nOK      gamma \[required\]: present \(jq 1\.7\.1\)\nPREREQ  0 required
head: ABSENT  beta \[optional\]: missing \(jq not found\) -> STEP-beta\nMISSING gamma \[required\]: missing \(jq not found\) -> STEP-gamma\nPREREQ  1 required
replace: <a tool found only through a relative PATH entry>
why: QA B2 on PR #538: shutil.which searched a relative PATH entry (here rel, from the current directory) and found rel/jq; src/lib/onpath.js searches absolute entries only, as every moved Node command does, so a current directory cannot decide which program runs. A tool found only through a relative or empty entry therefore reads missing: a false red (exit 1), never a false OK. docs/prerequisites.md says so.

head: "code": 1
replace: "code": <0 with the relative entry searched, 1 without>
why: The exit code of the entry above: the required gamma item is found through the relative entry on the base (exit 0) and missing on the head (exit 1).

head: present \(git 2\.3\.4\)
replace: present (git <the version a probe child reports>)
why: A narrowing (lens F1 on PR #538): prerequisites.py ran every probe child (git, gh, terraform, each --version) with the caller's whole environment, so SONAR_TOKEN and TFC_API_TOKEN reached them. The Node check removes every variable a declaration item names as its auth.env before it starts a probe; the token is read only by this process, for its own GET. The case's git shim reports 9.9.9 when it can see a token and 2.3.4 when it cannot, so the base shows the token passed on and the head shows it withheld. test/check/prerequisites.test.js holds the same property with logging shims.

replace: <a project AGENTS.md that is not UTF-8: reported, not a traceback>
why: merge_authority.check_project read the project's AGENTS.md with read_text(encoding='utf-8') and caught only OSError, so a brief that is not UTF-8 raised UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError) out of mhw check: a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1, with no PROJECT line. The Node check catches the decode error and reports it as a finding on stdout (next entry). The exit code is 1 on both sides and is compared.

head: PROJECT merge authority: FAIL the AGENTS\.md at <TMP>/work/p is not readable UTF-8; the project brief must declare its merge-authority block\n$
replace: <the PROJECT line for an AGENTS.md that is not UTF-8>
why: The other half of the entry above: where workstation.py stopped with a traceback, the Node check prints one PROJECT FAIL line naming the brief as not readable UTF-8, after the prerequisites section, in the place every other project finding is printed. It is a finding (exit 1), not a fail-closed exit 2, because the installed contract was read and only the project's own file is at fault, as a missing AGENTS.md already was.

#503 (S25 of #470) deleted global/install.sh: the METHOD line the working-method step prints when the method is not installed named it as the second way to opt in ('./mhw install --method, or install.sh --method'), a pointer to a file that no longer exists. It now names `install --method` only. The rest of the line, and every other line, is compared unchanged.

head: , pattern-check\.js(?=[,\n])
why: #588: the admin layer's summary lines (ADMIN MISSING, DRIFT or STAMP <names>) name the fixed-pattern check's file among the others; that one name is taken out of the head side, so the line and its other names are still compared. Applied before the entry that drops whole lines naming the check's files.

base: the admin layer differs from this checkout: \d+ target\(s\)
head: the admin layer differs from this checkout: \d+ target\(s\)
replace: the admin layer differs from this checkout: <N> target(s)
why: #588: the admin layer's count of differing targets grows by the fixed-pattern check's file (bin/hook/src/hooks/pattern-check.js), so it is read as <N> on both sides; the names of the differing targets are still compared on the ADMIN lines that follow.

#588 (the fixed-pattern check; ADR-0033 and ADR-0035 decision 7 amendments of 2026-11-23): mhw install also installs the check's script and core under <data dir>/pattern-check, its own Kiro hook file and, in the admin layer, bin/hook/src/hooks/pattern-check.js. Each line the head prints that names one of those files (an OK, MISSING, WROTE, REMOVED, SKIP or STAMP line of --check, install or uninstall) is taken out of the head side; nothing else in the line set changes, and every other line is still compared. test/hooks/pattern-check-install.test.js and test/install/admin.test.js hold those files and lines.

#600 (the CLI native baseline PRD, slice 2b; ADR-0033 and ADR-0035 decision 7, 2026-11-23 amendments): `mhw hook prompt` left the CLI, and with it the Kiro CLI V3 hook file that ran it, ~/.kiro/hooks/personal-multi-harness-workstation-configuration-paste-filter.json. Install no longer writes or checks it (it retires one an earlier release left), so every line naming it in the original's transcript (MISSING, OK, DRIFT, WOULD WRITE, REMOVED) is taken out of the base side here; the fixed-pattern check's own Kiro file carries the prompt half (its lines are taken out of the head by the #588 entry). Every other line is still compared.

#600: the admin layer no longer stages `mhw hook prompt`'s entry and module (bin/hook/src/commands/hook-entry.js and hook-prompt.js; an --apply deletes them as legacy files), so the original's lines naming either file, and the two names in its summary lines, are taken out of the base side. The count of differing targets is already normalised.

#600: the admin layer no longer stages `mhw hook prompt`'s entry and module (bin/hook/src/commands/hook-entry.js and hook-prompt.js; an --apply deletes them as legacy files), so the original's lines naming either file, and the two names in its summary lines, are taken out of the base side. The count of differing targets is already normalised.

#590 (the CLI native baseline PRD, slice 4): the paste wrapper is removed, so install no longer writes or checks its shell snippet (paste-filter.sh) or its start-up block, and prints no NOTE asking the owner to add the start-up line by hand. `mhw check` therefore prints no OK, MISSING or DRIFT line for either; one an earlier install left is named STALE and removed by install (test/install/install-user.test.js, test/render/shell-rc.test.js). Every such line is taken out of the original's side.
#590: with the snippet and the start-up block no longer install targets, a HOME without them has no drift in the 'paste wrapper' category, so a drift list no longer names it.

head: \b177(?= deny-floor)|\b177(?=/177 )|(?<=/)177\b
why: #593 (the CLI native baseline PRD, slice 7a; ADR-0048, the owner's decision «Abrir o deny»): the eight `gh api -X|--method POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE` entries left global/deny-floor.conf, so every count of the floor's rules this view prints moved by eight, the Claude Code and Kiro counts from 185 to 177 and the Codex prefix rules from 161 to 153. Only those counts, in the positions the floor lines print them, are read as <N> on both sides; every other word of each line is still compared, and test/render/gh-api.test.js holds that the floor lists no gh api write.

base: (?<=narrow tier, )10(?= allow rules)|(?<=Claude Code: default \(none set\), )10(?= allow rules)|(?<=agent workstation, )10(?= trusted commands)
head: (?<=narrow tier, )11(?= allow rules)|(?<=Claude Code: default \(none set\), )11(?= allow rules)|(?<=agent workstation, )11(?= trusted commands)
why: #593 (ADR-0048, «Mover para o baseline»): install renders the baseline's gh api rule set (global/gh-api.conf) beside the allow list in every tier, so the narrow Claude Code allow list has one more rule, `Bash(gh api repos/*/milestones*)`, and the Kiro agent one more trusted command, the milestone pattern. Only the narrow-tier Claude Code count and the Kiro count are read as <N> on both sides; test/render/gh-api.test.js and test/render/allow-list.test.js hold the rules themselves.

#593 (ADR-0048): install now reports the retirement of the owner's hand-kept `Bash(gh api:*)` deny, and on a settings file without one it prints `OK ... no hand-kept Bash(gh api:*) deny`. That one line is taken out of the head side; every other line is still compared, and test/render/gh-api.test.js holds the retirement, its backup and its restore.
